- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- If sentiment turns positive sharply (e.g., > 0.3) after a dip, model often over-optimizes; cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true breakout.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecasted peaks in that window.  
- When sentiment shows mean-reversion signals (e.g., alternating +/– 0.2), model often fails to correct; apply a 0.3–0.7% downward bias to mid-term forecasts.  
- Model over-anticipates short-term momentum (e.g., 3–5 day moves) when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in such periods.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, model is lagging; apply 1–2% upward correction to next forecast horizon.
